$note: Written for whoever is sourcing pictures, not for the pipeline. The reel renders without any of these: every line here is either drawn procedurally or stated in type, and each entry says which. BLOCKING means the line is about something type cannot depict and no drawing covers it.

wanted.says: A Roman harbour wall poured into the sea in 40 BC still stands in the surf.
wanted.subject: geography
wanted.described: a weathered concrete mole running into grey-green water
wanted.purpose: establish where this is and how the parts of it stand relative to each other
wanted.composition: high or aerial view with a clear horizon; the relation between the two sides must be legible
wanted.orientation: landscape source, croppable to 9:16 without losing the relation
wanted.constraints: the actual named place; contemporary imagery is acceptable unless the line dates it
wanted.substitutes: a comparable coastline of the same character, LABELLED as illustrative and not as the place
wanted.reject: tourist framing, visible modern signage where the line is historical, any view that hides the relation the sentence is about

wanted.says: Modern marine concrete cracks and fails in fifty years. Often in thirty.
wanted.subject: romanConcrete
wanted.described: spalled modern concrete with rusted reinforcement showing
wanted.purpose: show the substance itself at a scale where its structure is visible
wanted.composition: macro or section; the structure is the subject, not the object it came from
wanted.constraints: the actual material named; a sample of the same class only if labelled
wanted.substitutes: a published micrograph or core sample photograph with its source credited
wanted.reject: a generic texture, a rendered material, anything where the structure cannot be seen
